label_origin: Fresh source-only judgments authored by the delegated labeling agent before any baseline/candidate output for this pack exists or is inspected. Not human adjudication or independently verified real-world truth.

scoring_protocol.unit: A fixed-context case, with separate judgments for story relationship, event identity, semantic coverage, attribution/scope and evidence-field correctness.
scoring_protocol.request_budget: Exactly three bounded case requests per arm can carry all 14 source versions. Do not spend one model request per archived day. The same source cards and ordering must be used for baseline and candidate.
scoring_protocol.blindness: Do not expose labels or reader-question answers to evaluated models. Do not tune labels after seeing outputs. Root must review labels against the frozen sources before starting either arm.
scoring_protocol.required: Score a missing required reader-answer assertion as a meaningful omission only if the output is expected to answer that case. Score separate, material overstatement/attribution errors even when the central fact is present.
scoring_protocol.important_context: These details improve completeness. Apply the stated conditions rather than requiring every background sentence in a compact output.
scoring_protocol.conditional: Score only when the model chooses to discuss that claim or explanatory dimension. Absence alone is not a failure.
scoring_protocol.allowed_abstention: Any relationship explicitly listed as unscored/ambiguous is excluded from correctness denominators. Unlisted pairs should not be automatically converted to hard gold unless implied by an explicitly scored same/different story group.
scoring_protocol.story_vs_event: Articles can belong to one ongoing matter while describing different developments. Do not score a flexible event granularity choice as a story continuity failure.
scoring_protocol.citation_scope: Evidence spans identify exact title or normalized text, using zero-based Python Unicode character offsets [start,end). A headline-only element needs title evidence or an alternative supplied source text that actually states it. A URL alone is never evidence of a proposition.
scoring_protocol.no_exhaustiveness_claim: This is a deliberately selected 3-case supplement, not a random sample, production quality rate, full-history retrieval test or estimate of general accuracy.
scoring_protocol.no_checklist_fabrication: No explicit publisher correction is present. Do not require one. Claims/denials within an article are not automatically disagreement between publishers.
scoring_protocol.changes: If root finds a source-only labeling mistake before model runs, make a new documented label version and freeze new hashes. After any output inspection, do not silently revise this pack or use retrospective labels as if they were blind.

cases.purpose: Keep a specific lawsuit coherent across a gap exceeding 14 days while rejecting another OpenAI lawsuit as a competing story.

same_story_groups.matter: Musk’s challenge to OpenAI’s departure from its original nonprofit mission.
OpenAI’s handling of the Tumbler Ridge shooter’s account, the apology and families’ negligence lawsuits.

story_relationships.rationale: The Musk matter repeats the named claimant, OpenAI, donated funds and nonprofit-to-profit dispute in the April 29 and May 18 text. The competitor names a Canadian shooting, victim families, notification of authorities and negligence claims. Shared OpenAI/Altman, courts or litigation do not make these one matter.

evidence.quote: Musk beweert dat hij door Altman is misleid toen hij in de beginjaren van OpenAI geld doneerde.
Met de rechtszaak wil Musk bereiken dat OpenAI's aanpassing naar een op winst gericht bedrijf wordt teruggedraaid.
Elon Musk heeft de rechtszaak die hij tegen OpenAI aanspande verloren.

De miljardair had het bedrijf van topman Sam Altman voor de rechter gesleept omdat hij er geld aan doneerde en het er niet mee eens is dat het een bedrijf is geworden dat winst maakt in plaats van een non-profit onderzoeksbedrijf.

Families of seven victims of a mass shooting at a secondary school in British Columbia are suing OpenAI and the company’s CEO for negligence after it failed to alert authorities to the shooter’s troubling conversations with ChatGPT.

The head of OpenAI has written a letter apologizing that his company didn’t alert law enforcement about the online behavior of a person who shot and killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia.

temporal_obligation.expected: An age cutoff alone must not split the current outcome into a new unrelated story. The supplied source text supports the continuation; unseen intervening events must not be invented.

event_identity.definition: Story continuity is scored separately from whether two source cards describe one concrete development.

same_event_groups.description: May 18 loss of the Musk lawsuit on timeliness grounds.

different_event_pairs.reason: An apology/letter and subsequently filed negligence lawsuits are distinct developments within the Tumbler Ridge matter.

unscored.reason: Both explain the Musk dispute. The brief BBC source does not establish a precise court session or bounded event shared with the NOS explainer; neither a same-event nor a different-event label is required.

event_identity.current_versus_prior: The May 18 outcome is a new development in the older Musk matter, not a duplicate of the prior explanatory coverage.

cases.purpose: Separate two named matters involving Starmer and preserve the procedural status and attribution of each.

same_story_groups.matter: Proposed parliamentary investigation of Starmer over Mandelson’s appointment/vetting and whether Parliament was misled.
Trial over arson attacks on Starmer-linked properties and a car.

story_relationships.rationale: A parliamentary motion about Mandelson’s appointment and a criminal arson trial have different conduct, parties and procedural forums. The shared Starmer name and close publication dates are not a basis to merge.

evidence.quote: Starmer faces vote on inquiry over Mandelson vetting claims
In het parlement wist de motie hiervoor geen meerderheid te behalen.

Uit het onderzoek had duidelijk moeten worden of de sociaaldemocraat Starmer het Lagerhuis mogelijk bewust of onbewust heeft misleid in de affaire rond de benoeming van Peter Mandelson als ambassadeur in de Verenigde Staten.
Two buildings and a car linked to Prime Minister Keir Starmer of Britain were set afire last year.
The incident is one of a series of arson attacks that took place in May last year on property linked to Keir Starmer, which three men with links to Ukraine are accused of targeting.

different_event_pairs.reason: The parliamentary vote outcome and court testimony about an arson attack are different concrete developments as well as different stories.

unscored.reason: The earlier item anticipates a vote and the later item reports a motion failing. They certainly advance the same inquiry matter. Whether an event representation treats anticipation and outcome as one vote lifecycle or separate developments is not scored.

The snippets describe prosecutorial/court allegations on the same day in the arson matter, but do not establish that the accounts come from the identical hearing session or the same specific testimony. Same story is scored; exact event identity is not.

event_identity.allowed_granularity: The April 30 witness account can be represented as a new trial development or as additional evidence within a continuing trial event; do not score that representation choice as a story-link error.

expectations.assertion: The proposed investigation concerned whether Starmer misled the Commons over Mandelson’s appointment. Failure of the motion is not a criminal acquittal or a finding that nobody was misled.

cases.purpose: Use short RSS headlines as separately citeable evidence while respecting their attribution, scope and missing details.

same_story_groups.matter: Announced cap for most bus fares in England.
Charges over an alleged plan to manipulate water quality tests.
OpenAI’s report of its AI launching a cyberattack.

story_relationships.rationale: The supplied concrete developments concern separate policies, proceedings and incidents. Shared source and publication date establish no story relationship.
story_relationships.bounded_history_note: No prior sources are supplied here. This does not prove that any matter is new in the wider world.

different_event_pairs.reason: Bus policy and water-testing charges are different developments.
Bus policy and a reported AI cyberattack are different developments.
Water-testing charges and a reported AI cyberattack are different developments.
